fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, and most of my work has been building software and machine learning systems that real people use. Right now I work on applied ML and product at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I built major parts of the data and ML infrastructure for an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system: the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, the public detection API, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer for prioritizing alerts. I also built an LLM explanation layer using retrieval-augmented generation so analysts can act on what the system flags. The thing I care about there is operational usefulness, since an anomaly system that produces too many alerts creates a second problem instead of solving the first. Before that I worked with Intelehealth on AI and data systems for rural telemedicine, including an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard. I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence and shipped ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app, into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users.
